newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 per tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 per tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 a tonne lower on Thursday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.

London cocoa futures slumped early Thursday, as broad-based long liquidation pressured the market. LIFFE July cocoa was down 12 stg at the midday break, to 982 stg, just shy of key chart support at 980 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures ended down sharply, as speculative liquidation drove July to a three-week low. July fell $29 on the day, to $1,420, just off the session low of $1,418. Second-month September finished $27 lower, at $1,461, while the back months slumped $23 to $28.
Technically, traders pegged July key chart support at $1,412, followed by $1,404-$1,400.
On the fundamental front, world's largest cocoa bean processor Barry Callebaut forecasted the Ivory Coast's 1997/98 crop at 1.1 million tonnes and the 1996/97 crop at 1.14 million tonnes.
Callebaut expected Ghana's crop to come in at 330,000 tonnes this year and steady in 1997/98, while Indonesia should produce 330,000 tonnes this year and add 10 percent next year.
